title: MYP Extended Mathematics: How Many Criteria?
summary: MYP Extended Mathematics has four criteria, A to D. Learn how each is assessed, totaled internally, and applied in the 100-mark eAssessment.
body_markdown:
MYP Extended Mathematics has **four assessment criteria** , labelled **A, B, C and D** : Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts.


Standard and Extended Mathematics use the same criteria. Extended Mathematics differs through the greater breadth, depth and complexity of its content, not through an extra criterion. The distinction between classroom assessment and the external eAssessment is also important because they use different marking scales.


### The four MYP Extended Mathematics criteria


The IB describes the mathematics criteria as **equally weighted** . In school-based assessment, each has a maximum achievement level of **8** , producing a combined maximum of **32** .


Criterion Name What it measures Maximum internal level


**A** Knowing and understanding Selecting and applying appropriate mathematics to solve problems **8**


**B** Investigating patterns Identifying patterns, developing rules and justifying conclusions **8**


**C** Communicating Using correct notation, representations and logical organization **8**


**D** Applying mathematics in real-life contexts Modelling situations and evaluating mathematical results **8**


The[official IB mathematics subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/brochures-and-infographics/pdfs/myp-brief-mathematics-en.pdf) summarizes these criteria and the on-screen examination. RevisionDojo also provides a practical explanation of[MYP Mathematics Criteria A, B, C and D](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-math-criterion-a-b-c-d-explained-simply) .


### Criterion A: Knowing and understanding


Criterion A assesses whether you can select suitable mathematics and apply it successfully. Evidence may include accurate algebra, correct formula use and effective methods for familiar or unfamiliar problems.


Extended Mathematics questions can require more advanced techniques than the standard course, but they still assess Criterion A. A correct answer is valuable, although visible working may be needed to demonstrate the method fully.


### Criterion B: Investigating patterns


Criterion B concerns mathematical investigation. You may need to generate results, identify a pattern, formulate a general rule and justify why it works.


For example, observing that a sequence changes by successive odd numbers is only a starting point. A stronger response proposes a rule such as an=n2a_n=n^2

### Criterion C: Communicating


Criterion C assesses how effectively you present mathematics. Correct symbols, labelled graphs, suitable representations, coherent reasoning and a logical structure can all provide evidence.


Communication is not simply neat handwriting. An undefined variable, unsupported calculator result or graph without labelled axes can weaken a response even when the underlying idea is correct.


### Criterion D: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts


Criterion D assesses mathematical modelling in an authentic context. You identify relevant information, choose a strategy, solve the problem, and interpret and evaluate the result.


If a model predicts 18.718.7


18.7


buses, the practical answer may be **19 buses** . A complete response explains that decision and considers whether the model's assumptions are reasonable. RevisionDojo's guide to[how MYP Mathematics is assessed and revised](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-mathematics-is-assessed-and-how-to-revise-for-it) offers additional criterion-specific advice.


### How internal MYP Mathematics grading works


In classroom assessment, teachers award an achievement level for each criterion. The scale is **0 to 8** : levels 1 to 8 correspond to achievement descriptors, while 0 means the work has not reached the standard described by the first band.


Teachers use **best-fit judgment** based on the available evidence. A final criterion level is therefore not necessarily an average of every task score. Schools must provide opportunities to demonstrate every strand, while their assessment policies explain the exact reporting process.


A final set of levels might be:


Criterion Final achievement level


A: Knowing and understanding 7


B: Investigating patterns 6


C: Communicating 7


D: Applying mathematics in real-life contexts 5


**Total** **25 out of 32**


The school converts this total into a reported **1-to-7 grade** using its authorized reporting approach. Many MYP schools use a conversion in which 24--27 corresponds to grade 6, but students should confirm the table in their school's current assessment policy.


Crucially, **25 out of 32 is a criterion total, not 78.125% on an examination** . Criterion levels describe the quality of demonstrated achievement rather than ordinary test points.[RevisionDojo's guide to MYP grade boundaries](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-myp-grade-boundaries-understanding-the-1-7-scale) explains the 0--8, 0--32 and 1--7 scales further.


### How the MYP Extended Mathematics eAssessment works


The optional external **MYP Extended Mathematics eAssessment** is an on-screen examination taken at the end of MYP Year 5. The IB's[MYP assessment page](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/assessment-and-exams/) explains how external assessment can lead to MYP course results or contribute to the MYP Certificate.


The mathematics blueprint organizes the examination into three broad tasks:


Examination task Main criteria assessed Approximate task marks


Knowing and understanding A and C **31--35**


Investigating patterns B and C **31--35**


Applying mathematics in real-life contexts C and D **31--35**


**Whole examination** **A, B, C and D** **100**


Each criterion contributes **25 raw marks** across the examination. Criterion C appears across all three tasks, so clear communication matters throughout the paper rather than only in one extended response.


Context Scale before final grade Conversion


School-based assessment Four levels out of 8, totaling **32** School reporting process converts the total to 1--7


External eAssessment Raw marks totaling **100** IB session-specific boundaries convert the mark to 1--7


Students can use the[MYP Extended Mathematics resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-extended-mathematics) and[Extended Mathematics Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-extended-mathematics/questionbank) while identifying which criterion each response demonstrates.


### How eAssessment grade boundaries work


Official grade boundaries convert the external raw mark into a final grade from **1 to 7** . The IB establishes them for the relevant subject and examination session, so an earlier session's boundary is not guaranteed to remain unchanged.


For illustration only, suppose a student scores **72 out of 100** , with grade 6 beginning at 68 and grade 7 at 79. The result would be grade 6 because 68≤72<7968 \\leq 72 < 79

Coordinators should use official session documentation when interpreting results. Students should not convert mock percentages through the classroom 32-point table because the two systems assess different evidence.


The eAssessment result may contribute to the MYP Certificate. Under the IB's[grading and awards guidance](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/assessment-and-exams/grading-and-awards/) , the certificate has a maximum of **56 points** , and candidates must meet all certificate conditions.


### Common mistakes about the criteria


- **Assuming Extended Mathematics has extra criteria:** It uses the same four as standard mathematics.
- **Calling an 8 a final subject grade:** Eight is the maximum level for one criterion; subject grades run from 1 to 7.
- **Treating criterion levels as percentages:** A level 6 is descriptor-based, not automatically 75%.
- **Assigning Criterion C to one task:** Communication is assessed across all three eAssessment task types.
- **Using classroom boundaries externally:** Internal totals are out of 32; the eAssessment is marked out of 100.
- **Revising only Criterion A:** Investigation, communication and modelling are also formally assessed.


Effective revision should combine procedural questions, pattern investigations, clearly presented solutions and contextual modelling. After answering, ask which criterion evidence an examiner can actually see.


### Conclusion


MYP Extended Mathematics has **four equally weighted criteria** : A, Knowing and understanding; B, Investigating patterns; C, Communicating; and D, Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Internally, each has a maximum level of 8, while the external eAssessment allocates 25 raw marks to each criterion within a 100-mark examination.


Classroom criterion totals and external marks are not interchangeable. RevisionDojo's Questionbank, Study Notes, Flashcards and Jojo AI can support balanced practice across all four criteria.
